// diagnostic

L0105

Package export `{name}` is unreachable.

What

Package export `{name}` is unreachable.

Why

The package's explicit import graph and application roots contain no consumer for this package-scoped export; library `pub` remains open to external consumers.

Fix

remove the export, or rename `{name}` to `_{name}` when it is intentional.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning L0105: tests/ui_lint/liveness_unused_import.warn.

Warning [L0101] (unused_local_binding): local binding `dead` is never read.
  --> tests/ui_lint/liveness_unused_import.jet:10:5
    |
 10 |     dead :: 5
    |     ^^^^
 Why: a binding that no later expression reads adds dead code and may hide a computed result that should have been used.
 Fix: remove the binding when its initializer is side-effect free, or rename `dead` to `_dead` when the value must be computed.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L0101

Warning [L0103] (unused_import): import `files` is never used.
  --> tests/ui_lint/liveness_unused_import.jet:1:19
    |
  1 | use core.files as files
    |                   ^^^^^
 Why: an unused import adds a name and dependency to the file without contributing to checked code.
 Fix: remove the import, or rename `files` to `_files` when the import is intentionally kept.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L0103

Warning [L0105] (unreachable_export): package export `package_helper` is unreachable.

    |
  3 | pub(package) fn package_helper() {
    |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: the package's explicit import graph and application roots contain no consumer for this package-scoped export; library `pub` remains open to external consumers.
 Fix: remove the export, or rename `package_helper` to `_package_helper` when it is intentional.

Warning [L0104] (unused_private_fn): private function `unused_helper` is never called or used as a value.
  --> tests/ui_lint/liveness_unused_import.jet:6:4
    |
  6 | fn unused_helper() {
    |    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: a private function with no reachable reference is dead code; public functions stay exempt because other modules may use them.
 Fix: remove the function, or rename `unused_helper` to `_unused_helper` when it is intentional.
